title: this in Arrow Functions
concept: Arrow functions don't have their own this — they use the this from their enclosing scope

steps.title: Call user.greetRegular()
steps.explanation:
Call the `greetRegular` method on the `user` object.
At this moment, `this` inside `greetRegular` is `user`.
However, the `setTimeout` callback (a regular function) inside it will lose `this` when the Web API runs it 100ms later.

steps.title: Call user.greetArrow()
steps.explanation:
Call the `greetArrow` method.
At this moment, `this` inside `greetArrow` is also `user`.
The `setTimeout` callback (an arrow function) inside it will 'remember' this `this` value when it runs 100ms later.

steps.title: Callback Executes (Regular Function)
steps.explanation:
After 100ms, the callback from `greetRegular` runs.
This callback is a 'regular function', so it gets its own `this` when called.
The `this` of a callback called by `setTimeout` points to the global object (`window`), so `this.name` is `undefined`.
steps.keyInsight: A regular function callback's this is the global object.

steps.title: Callback Executes (Arrow Function)
steps.explanation:
Next, the callback from `greetArrow` runs.
An 'arrow function' doesn't create its own `this` — it uses the `this` from its lexical scope (where it was defined).
Here it refers to the `user` object, which is `greetArrow` method's `this`.
steps.keyInsight: Arrow function's this = my parent's this (inherited)

quiz.explanation:
Arrow functions use the this from their enclosing scope at the time of definition.
Even though it's defined as a method of obj, obj is not a scope, so the global this is used.

misconceptions.wrong: Arrow function's this refers to the parent object
misconceptions.correct:
No.
It refers to the enclosing **function** scope.
An object literal `{}` is not a scope.
misconceptions.why:
Objects don't act as scopes.
So an arrow function inside an object literal ends up pointing to the global (window).

misconceptions.wrong: You can change arrow function's this with call/apply/bind
misconceptions.correct:
Arrow function's this cannot be changed.
call/apply/bind are ignored.
misconceptions.why: Arrow functions use lexical this, so their binding is fixed.

keyTakeaway: Arrow function = no own this, uses the this from enclosing scope (lexical)
